title: Freight Report November 2026
summary: The freight market is heading into November with rates continuing to climb and capacity tightening across all three equipment types. But higher rates don't automatically mean healthier margins for carriers. Here's what to know as we head toward year-end.
body_markdown:
## Spot Rates Update


October data showed all three equipment types gaining ground, with DAT's national spot rates moving to $3.12/mile for van, $3.62/mile for flatbed, and $3.71/mile for reefer in its latest November snapshot.


The tightening capacity element is also important. During the last week of October, DAT reported load-to-truck ratios increasing across the big three equipment types, while truck postings fell and load postings increased.


Diesel averages are down slightly week over week, but remain a[substantial operating-cost](https://truenorthfleet.com/articles/business/fuel-economy-tips-to-offset-rising-fuel-prices) concern.


Source:[DAT Trendlines](https://iq.trendlines-prod.prod.dat.com/trendlines-legacy)


C.H. Robinson's October projections point to continued elevated rates into 2027, forecasting year-over-year increases in 2027. Its October report also highlighted persistent route-guide tension, rising failures, and tightening flatbed and reefer capacity in certain regions.


Source:[C.H. Robinson Freight Market Update](https://www.chrobinson.com/en-us/resources/insights-and-advisories/north-america-freight-insights/oct-2026-freight-market-update/na-truckload/)


Regional conditions remain uneven. The Pacific Northwest continues to experience tighter refrigerated capacity, while the Northeast has seen stronger flatbed demand tied to industrial, construction, and project freight.


## Load-to-Truck Ratio


DAT reported 10.2 load-to-truck ratio for dry van, pointing to tightening spot-market capacity heading into November, with flatbed showing the largest weekly increase in its load-to-truck ratio.


## November Outlook


[C.H. Robinson's latest outlook](https://www.chrobinson.com/en-us/resources/insights-and-advisories/north-america-freight-insights/oct-2026-freight-market-update/na-truckload/) points to continued capacity constraints, although conditions will vary by equipment and region. Its near-term assessment highlights:


- Dry van capacity remains relatively tight, with route-guide failures elevated despite some improvement since Labor Day.
- Reefer capacity is easing nationally as produce season winds down, although the Pacific Northwest remains tighter.
- Flatbed conditions are generally stabilizing seasonally, but Northeast capacity remains constrained by industrial, construction, and project-related freight.


Carriers should capitalize on stronger spot rates while keeping a close eye on operating expenses. Diesel remains spendy, and higher fuel and maintenance costs continue to put pressure on margins.
